name: paw-avatar
summary: A glass puppy head whose 15 agent states (idle, thinking, working, sleeping, error...) morph into each other; pose is a pure function of time, so it pauses, scrubs and exports frame-exact.

state.description: Which state to hold. One of idle, happy, excited, curious, thinking, working, focused, surprised, sleeping, wink, confused, sad, love, celebrating, listening.

speed.description: Time multiplier for the whole engine. Clamped to 0.1-10.

cycle.description: Seconds per state when walking every state in turn; 0 holds the chosen state.

deviations.what: The character is ours. Upstream's PROFILES arrays and its 14 states are frame-by-frame measurements of the x.ai bot; none of those numbers are here. The Paw head is authored as a union of disks with a flat bottom, each ear is a three-disk lobe on a rotating root, and the 15 states are ours.
deviations.why: Upstream's own README says its MIT licence covers the code, not the visual design it recreates. Porting the engine and authoring a new character is the only use of it that is ours to ship.

deviations.what: Poses interpolate the ear rig (angle, lift) and the silhouette is rebuilt from it each frame, instead of lerping two sampled radius arrays as upstream's blend() does.
deviations.why: A lerp between two traced outlines crossfades an ear; lerping the rig rotates it. Upstream has one body and no limbs, so the question never came up there.

deviations.what: Silhouettes are sampled at 96 angles, not upstream's 64, and everything below y = 0.84 head radii is clamped flat.
deviations.why: A drooping ear tip is thinner than anything on a single blob and blobs out at 64 samples. The flat bottom is the Paw sitting rather than floating, which a union of disks cannot give on its own.

deviations.what: Rest gaze is square on (yaw 0) where upstream's is a measured 3/4 view (yaw 28.49, pitch 28.62, roll -13), and eyefit.ts is not ported.
deviations.why: The Paw looks at the reader. Its eyes also sit at 0.33 head radii, deep inside the outline, so the eye-to-edge correction eyefit exists for has nothing to correct.

deviations.what: TypeScript ported to plain ES modules; the Vue component, decor.ts, cycles.ts, expressions.ts, skins.ts and all of src/ui are not ported.
deviations.why: paw-fx effects are framework-free vanilla with a mount() contract, and the skin is CSS custom properties rather than a JS skin table.
